title: Understanding data protection basics (SME data protection guide)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. GDPR principles (lawful, fair and transparent; purpose limitation; minimisation; accuracy; storage limitation; security; accountability); special category data such as health, biometric and genetic data generally prohibited unless an exception applies; criminal offence data under separate conditions.

title: Respect individuals' rights (SME data protection guide)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Eight rights (informed, access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, objection, not subject to solely automated decisions); respond within one month, extendable by two further months for complex requests with notice in the first month; usually free; identity checks where there is reasonable doubt.

title: Be compliant (SME data protection guide)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Written records of processing (purpose, data categories, recipients, transfers, storage period, security) available to the authority; organisations under 250 employees need not record purely occasional processing; DPIA required where processing is likely high risk, usually when two of nine criteria apply; prior consultation if residual risk stays high; accountability.

title: Data breaches (SME data protection guide)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Definition of a personal data breach; notify the authority within 72 hours unless unlikely to pose a risk, with reasons for any delay; tell individuals without undue delay when high risk; document every breach, reported or not; processors tell the controller without undue delay.

title: Data controller or data processor (SME data protection guide)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Controller decides purposes and means; processor acts on instructions; required contract terms (instructions, confidentiality, security, sub-processor authorisation, help with rights, breaches and DPIAs, deletion or return, information and audits); sub-processors only with prior written authorisation and the same protections.

title: Standard contractual clauses (SCC)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. SCCs are pre-approved contract terms for transfers outside the EU/EEA; modernised SCCs adopted 4 June 2021 replacing three older sets; Q&As dated 25 May 2022; further sets in development.

title: Adequacy decisions
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Countries with adequacy decisions; the UK GDPR and LED decisions renewed on 19 December 2025; the United States covered for commercial organisations in the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (decision of 10 July 2023, first review report 9 October 2024).

title: Data protection
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018 govern use of personal data; data protection principles; stronger protection for sensitive information; individuals' rights including access, erasure, objection and rights about automated decisions; the ICO named as the body for advice and complaints.

title: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025: plans for commencement
publisher: GOV.UK (Department for Science, Innovation and Technology)
supports: Opened with WebFetch; page updated 12 October 2026. Royal Assent 19 June 2025; most Part 5 data protection and privacy provisions commenced 5 February 2026; complaints-handling duty planned for about 12 months after Royal Assent; Information Commissioner's functions transferred to the Information Commission on 30 September 2026.

title: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA)
publisher: State of California Department of Justice, Office of the Attorney General
supports: Opened with WebFetch; page updated 28 August 2026. Who the law covers (for-profit businesses meeting one of three thresholds); rights to know, delete, opt out of sale or sharing, correct, limit use of sensitive data and non-discrimination; 45 calendar days to respond, extendable by 45; opt-outs within 15 business days; Global Privacy Control must be honoured.

title: California finalizes regulations to strengthen consumers' privacy (23 September 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Regulations on cybersecurity audits, risk assessments, ADMT, insurance and CCPA updates take effect 1 January 2026; risk assessment compliance from 1 January 2026 with attestations due by 1 April 2028; ADMT duties from 1 January 2027; cybersecurity audit certifications due 1 April 2028, 2029 or 2030 by revenue tier.

title: CCPA monetary thresholds and penalties adjusted for 2025 (17 December 2024)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. From 1 January 2025 the revenue threshold rose from $25,000,000 to $26,625,000; administrative fines and civil penalties rose to $2,663 per violation and $7,988 for intentional violations or those involving consumers under 16.

title: SOC 2: SOC for Service Organizations, Trust Services Criteria
supports: Opened with WebFetch. SOC services are provided by CPAs and give users information to assess the risks of outsourcing; trust services categories security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy; exposure drafts of proposed 2027 SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria and Description Criteria dated 26 October 2026; AICPA notice that it is looking into allegations about a compliance vendor's practices.

title: 2017 Trust Services Criteria (With Revised Points of Focus, 2022)
supports: Opened with WebFetch; resource page dated 30 September 2023. The control criteria practitioners use to evaluate and report on controls in SOC 2 examinations, in five categories.

title: SOC 2 Reporting on an Examination of Controls at a Service Organization (guide)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The AICPA guide for CPAs performing SOC 2 and SOC 3 examinations, updated as of 15 October 2022; customers and business partners commonly ask service organisations for a SOC 2 report.

title: Ethics Staff Insights: business arrangements with SOC tool providers (13 April 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. AICPA members increasingly enter business arrangements with SOC 2 tool providers, which can threaten compliance with the Code of Professional Conduct, including independence and objectivity.

title: ISO/IEC 27001 Information Security Management System
supports: Opened with WebFetch (iso.org blocks automated fetches). ISO/IEC 27001 is the information security management system standard, risk-based and usable by any organisation; certification requires meeting Clauses 4 to 10 and involves a two-stage audit; the page refers to the 2022 edition.

title: Just published: PCI DSS v4.0.1
supports: Opened with WebFetch. PCI DSS v4.0.1 published 11 June 2024 as a limited revision with no added or removed requirements; v4.0 retired 31 December 2024; future-dated requirements effective 31 March 2025.

title: FAQ clarifies new SAQ A eligibility criteria for e-commerce merchants
supports: Opened with WebFetch. FAQ 1588 published 28 February 2025: SAQ A merchants with an embedded payment page or form (such as an iframe) must confirm the site is not susceptible to script attacks, through Requirements 6.4.3 and 11.6.1 or confirmation from their compliant provider; not applicable to redirects or full outsourcing; effective 1 April 2025.

title: Merchant resources
supports: Opened with WebFetch. PCI DSS is a baseline of technical and operational requirements for entities handling cardholder data; payment brands and acquirers decide validation requirements; SAQs are self-assessment tools for eligible merchants and service providers; each payment brand runs its own compliance programme.

title: AI Act (regulatory framework for AI)
publisher: European Commission, Shaping Europe's digital future
supports: Opened with WebFetch; page updated 19 October 2026. Risk tiers; in force 1 August 2024; prohibitions and AI literacy 2 February 2025; general-purpose AI 2 August 2025; transparency rules August 2026; nudification ban December 2026; AI Omnibus in force 27 July 2026 moved Annex III high-risk rules to 2 December 2027 and product-embedded high-risk rules to 2 August 2028.

title: Article 4: AI literacy
publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Current text: providers and deployers take measures to support AI literacy of staff and others using AI on their behalf, suited to their knowledge and the context; no specific literacy level must be guaranteed; the Commission and member states support this, especially for SMEs.

title: Article 99: Penalties
publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Maximum fines: EUR 35 million or 7% for prohibited practices; EUR 15 million or 3% for other obligations; EUR 7.5 million or 1% for incorrect information; for SMEs and start-ups the lower of the two figures applies.

title: NIST releases version 2.0 of landmark Cybersecurity Framework
publisher: US National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports: Opened with WebFetch. CSF 2.0 released 26 February 2024; six functions Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover and the new Govern; aimed at organisations of all sizes and sectors; quick-start guides for small businesses.

title: Cyber Essentials overview
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The UK government's recommended minimum standard; five technical controls (firewalls, secure configuration, security update management, user access control, malware protection); Cyber Essentials Plus adds independent technical testing; certification through IASME, the NCSC's delivery partner, or an IASME-licensed certification body.

title: Confirmation statement guidance
supports: Opened with WebFetch; page updated 21 April 2026. Every company files at least one confirmation statement every 12 months, up to 14 days after the review period ends; late filing can bring a fine of up to 5,000 pounds and possible strike-off; a statement that intended future activities are lawful is required.

title: Verify your identity for Companies House
supports: Opened with WebFetch; page updated 30 April 2026. Directors and people with significant control must verify their identity; a legal requirement from 18 November 2025 with a 12-month transition to individual due dates; verify through GOV.UK One Login or an Authorised Corporate Service Provider.

title: Beneficial ownership information reporting
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A final rule dated 11 August 2026, effective 14 August 2026, keeps US companies exempt from BOI reporting; foreign companies registered to do business in a US state or tribal jurisdiction still report, within 30 days of registration for those registered after 26 March 2025.

title: The IIA's Three Lines Model: an update of the Three Lines of Defense
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The 2020 model explains how governing body, management and internal audit roles work together on governance and risk; updated September 2024 for the Global Internal Audit Standards glossary; now marked as superseded by a newer statement of position.

title: UK Corporate Governance Code
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The 2024 Code applies to financial years from 1 January 2025, with Provision 29 from 1 January 2026; it covers listed commercial companies and closed-ended investment funds on a comply or explain basis; private companies are not bound, and the Wates Principles offer a framework for large private companies.
